titulo: Partizip I and II as adjectives: Partizip I as an adjective

aula.titulo: Partizip I and II as adjectives
aula.objetivo: Use the Partizip II (gekochte Eier, ein verlorener Schlüssel, die gestiegenen Preise) and the Partizip I (lachend, die spielenden Kinder) as adjectives, with the right ending and the right meaning (passive and completed, active and completed, or active and simultaneous).

blocos.titulo: The Partizip I as an adjective, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the PARTIZIP I is formed with the INFINITIVE + «-D»: lachen → lachend; laufen → laufend; schlafen → schlafend; spielen → spielend. (It corresponds to the English "-ing" form: laughing, running, sleeping, playing.) STEP 2: the MEANING is ACTIVE and SIMULTANEOUS: «das schlafende Kind» is the child WHO IS SLEEPING; «die spielenden Kinder», the children who are playing. STEP 3: before the noun, it is declined like an adjective: «ein lachendes Kind», «die spielenden Kinder», «fließendes Wasser». STEP 4: it can work as an ADVERB, without an ending: «Er kam lachend herein» (he came in laughing). STEP 5: it appears in fixed expressions: «laufende Kosten» (running costs), «steigende Preise» (rising prices), «fließend Deutsch sprechen» (to speak German fluently). STEP 6: compare: Partizip I (active, happening) versus Partizip II (passive, completed): «das kochende Wasser» (the boiling water) versus «das gekochte Ei» (the boiled egg).

tabela.example: das kochende Wasser × das gekochte Ei

blocos.enunciado: Describe 6 scenes with Partizip I: «das schlafende Baby, die spielenden Kinder, fließendes Wasser …»
Write 6 sentences with Partizip II as an adjective, before the noun and after «sein».
